purpose: The reviewed commit of every plugin that a profile template enables, one entry each: the tag it resolves to where the template names a tag, and a recorded exception where it cannot be held to one. Claude Code applies a commit pin only from a plugin entry of a marketplace.json, never from a marketplace source (stage 2 lifts these entries into a catalog-owned marketplace whose plugin entries carry the sha); until then this record is what the template test and adoption/bootstrap.md step 4a hold the templates and the host to.

plugins.tag_resolution: receipts/tag-resolution.txt: refs/tags/v0.10.0^{} of jarrodwatts/claude-hud (an annotated tag; its peeled commit)
receipts/tag-resolution.txt: refs/tags/v1.0.6 of openai/codex-plugin-cc (a lightweight tag; the commit)

exception.reason: The marketplace source names no ref, so Claude Code installs the tip of the default branch. The reviewed commit is on no tag: the newest tag of the plugin's version, v1.0.169, resolves to a commit 133 commits older, with different bundled files, so naming that tag would change the content. A marketplace source takes a ref and never a sha, so the commit can be held only by a plugin entry of a marketplace.json that the catalog owns (stage 2).
exception.content_rule: adoption/bootstrap.md step 4a: an installed commit passes when GitHub's compare reports it ahead of the reviewed commit with stats.json as the only changed file

plugins.reason: A built-in mod of the client (adoption/new-wsl/client-config-map.json cites its page): it is versioned with the client, which the profile pins by version, and has no marketplace source to pin.

sources.claim: A plugin entry of a marketplace.json carries ref and sha (github, url and git-subdir sources); sha is a full 40-character lowercase commit and is checked out when both are set
A marketplace source (extraKnownMarketplaces, strictKnownMarketplaces) carries repo, ref, path and sparsePaths, and no sha
Pinning a plugin to a commit is a client feature since the changelog's pinning entry
The vendor's own marketplace sets sha on every external plugin entry
